title: Print proof
description: Inspect a hand-colored bird engraving and its luminance proof through one calibrated camera, even when the images have different raster dimensions.
useCase: Compare print proofs, retouches or imaging channels at matching world coordinates rather than unrelated image-pixel offsets.
interaction: Drag either image to move both views. Zoom with the buttons, double-click a view, or use arrow keys, plus, minus and Home. Escape cancels an active drag.

assets.description: Luminance conversion of the same engraving at 1400 px width
Luminance conversion of the same engraving at 2100 px width

reducedMotion: Pan follows direct input; release inertia is disabled. Keyboard and zoom controls update immediately. Host pause cancels release motion and disables input. Cancelling a drag or deactivating the host restores its starting camera.
limitations: The two images are known aligned derivatives of one public-domain engraving. No automatic image registration, pinch-to-zoom or color-managed printer simulation is provided.
look: A precise charcoal proofing surface with blue-and-ochre bird engraving detail beside its monochrome companion, paired white reticles, source-pixel coordinates and quiet zoom controls.
motion: Both image transforms derive from the same normalized world center and scale. Drag release coasts by a bounded amount; changing pane preserves the same camera. Different raster sizes produce different pixel readouts for the same physical feature.
adapt: Replace the color and proof assets with calibrated images of the same extent. `RATIO` describes that extent; `bounded` clamps the shared `Camera` to the visible image area. `maxZoom`, `companionRatio`, `panSettleMs` and `showCorrespondence` expose the supported controls.
